maria.g: Heads up — starting ~10:30 UTC we saw a spike in SAML assertion replay detections (~0.3% of logins) after the KMS alias rotate. A number of RBAC changes were rolled at 10:25. Anyone else seeing this? Correlation ids: c0ffee42.. :eyes:
aj: I see it too in prod and staging traces. Logs show `Assertion replay detected` with identical InResponseTo. Sample log: `authn-proxy[pid=2234] ERROR assertion_replay id=abcd1234 in_response_to=resp-77`
samir: Can you paste a redacted SAML response? Also confirm whether the KMS alias rotation was an alias swap or a rewrap job. Clock skew could make replay heuristics misfire.
maria.g: We rotated alias `alias/extid-main` -> `alias/extid-main-v2` at 10:20 UTC. RBAC rollout at 10:25 touched authn-proxy config. Here's a redacted snippet from SAML: `<samlp:Response InResponseTo="resp-77" IssueInstant="2026-04-24T10:29:51Z">...<SubjectConfirmationData NotOnOrAfter="2026-04-24T10:30:21Z"/></samlp:Response>`
devin: Quick checklist: 1) check JWKS kid rollover 2) ensure replay_cache_ttl not accidentally shortened 3) search audit logs for SCIM deprovision churn 4) verify KMS rewrap completion. I'll run queries.
sec-bot: incident created: #incident-3194 assertion-replay-surge (severity: low -> medium).
aj: Minimal repro: POST same SAML response to `/sso/saml/acs` twice within 30s -> second attempt flagged as replay. Found `replay_cache_ttl: 5s` in config under commit `c7f9a2`. That TTL is too low.
samir: That change came from RBAC rollout branch — it was supposed to be `50s`. Looks like a merge conflict resolution bug. Rolling back on staging now. @oncall can you patch prod? Low blast radius but impacts login UX for some users.
oncall: patch deploying in ~2m to canary (10% auth traffic). Watching auth success rate and replay metric.
maria.g: Also seeing a small cluster of SCIM deprovision failures around the same window: ~12 failed deprovisions with `KmsDecryptError 403`. Could be related to alias swap timing.
devin: Confirmed. SCIM service logs: `scim-service error: kms:Decrypt failed: NotFound for key arn:aws:kms:...:alias/extid-main` — seems alias repointed before async rewrap/backfill completed. We have write-after-read gap.
aj: Triage note (vuln): no signs of token leakage or attack. This looks operational. Recommended mitigations: add pre-rotate verification, enforce replay_cache_ttl >= 30s, and add canary for alias switch. I'll file follow-ups.
maria.g: Can we add an audit alert rule: if `scim.kms.decrypt.failures` > 5 within 1m, page sec oncall? And add metric for `sso.assertion.replay_rate` spike threshold.
oncall: Done — created alert and temporary suppression for noisy legacy clients. Canary is green; spike returned to baseline ~5m after patch.
sec-bot: task created: `sso/replay-ttl-hardening`, `scim/kms-pre-rotate-checklist`, `rbac/merge-conflict-checks`.
maria.g: Thanks team. We'll keep incident closed but open a short postmortem covering root cause (bad TTL merge + alias swap ordering) and timeline.
